Subject: RE: Post-call: FinEx performance & throughput SLOs - sizing draft + next steps

Hi all —

Attached is a first-pass throughput sizing note (summary below) — attachment includes assumptions, tokens/sec calculations, and recommended Dedicated configuration.

Key assumptions (from FinEx data):
- Median tokens per response: 980; 95th: 1,450; average token generation time: ~7-9ms per token on our optimized model at target latency
- Streaming fraction: 85% (continuous streaming)
- Peak QPS: 250 (10-15 minute bursts), steady 40 QPS
- Concurrency: average 6 concurrent streams per client during spikes

Sizing summary (baseline):
- Target P95 latency <=150ms (streaming): recommend 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (or 8xH100-80GB with quantized model) for a single Dedicated cluster to meet peak QPS with headroom for 1.5x unexpected spike.
- Tokens/sec required at peak (conservative):
  - Compute tokens/sec = peak_QPS * median_tokens = 250 * 980 = 245,000 tokens/sec
  - With 95th-size bursts: 250 * 1450 = 362,500 tokens/sec
- Model throughput measured on our bench: ~60k tokens/sec per A100-80GB for the target model (with streaming optimizations). So baseline compute devices needed: 
  - For median: 245k / 60k = ~4.1 -> 5 GPUs for comfortable headroom
  - For 95th burst: 362.5k / 60k = ~6.04 -> recommend 7-8 GPUs if you need to guarantee 95th under sustained peak
- Autoscaling: we recommend 4 GPUs minimum with burst pool autoscale to +4 GPUs during market open spikes (automated by QPS thresholds).

Tradeoffs / notes:
- If FinEx can accept best-effort handling of 95th bursts (i.e., occasional slight queuing or fallback to smaller model), baseline 4 GPUs gives good cost/latency for median traffic and saves ~30% capex.
- Quantized variants and model compilation for H100 pathways can increase tokens/sec per device by ~1.6x in some workloads; we can run a quick perf test if you provide a representative model binary and tokenized samples.

Requested next inputs to finalize numbers: 
1) A short window (2-4 hours) where FinEx can accept baseline traffic mirroring for an A/B perf test so we can benchmark actual tokens/sec on your payload.
2) Confirmation on tolerance for 95th percentile under sustained peak (i.e., strict guarantee vs best-effort).

Attaching the sizing PDF and a simple cost table (reserved vs on-demand) per Neha's ask.

Thanks — Rafael
